text:
Predicates:
MachineLearningAlgorithm(x) ::: x is a machine learning algorithm.
SupervisedLearning(x) ::: x is a supervised learning algorithm.
UnsupervisedLearning(x) ::: x is an unsupervised learning algorithm.
ReinforcementLearning(x) ::: x is a reinforcement learning algorithm.
RequiresLabelledData(x) ::: x requires labelled data.
TextSummarizationModel(y) ::: y is a text summarization model.
StateOfTheArt(y) ::: y is a state-of-the-art model.
TrainedWith(x, y) ::: y is trained with x.
Premises:
∀x (MachineLearningAlgorithm(x) → (SupervisedLearning(x) ∨ UnsupervisedLearning(x) ∨ ReinforcementLearning(x))) ::: Machine Learning algorithms can be categorized as supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and reinforcement learning.
∀x (UnsupervisedLearning(x) → ¬RequiresLabelledData(x)) ::: Unsupervised learning doesn't require labelled data.
∃x ∃y (StateOfTheArt(y) ∧ TextSummarizationModel(y) ∧ TrainedWith(x, y)) ::: The state-of-the-art text summarization model is trained with machine learning algorithms.
¬∃x (ReinforcementLearning(x) ∧ TrainedWith(x, stateOfTheArtTextSummarizationModel)) ::: Reinforcement learning is not used to train the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
∀x (TrainedWith(x, stateOfTheArtTextSummarizationModel) → RequiresLabelledData(x)) ::: The Machine Learning algorithm for training text summarization model requires labelled data.
Conclusion:
∃x (UnsupervisedLearning(x) ∧ TrainedWith(x, stateOfTheArtTextSummarizationModel)) ::: Unsupervised learning is used to train the state-of-the-art text summarization model.
